articles.title: Iraqi leader's planned crackdown on pro-Iran militias is riskiest move yet
articles.description: By Ahmed Rasheed and Michael GeorgyBAGHDAD/DUBAI Nov 17 (Reuters) - Just six months after coming to power as a political novice, Iraq's Prime Minister Alial-Zaidi is planning his riskiest move yet: directly confronting the heavily armed Shi'ite militias that function as proxies of Iran.The 41-year-old businessman-turned-politician has told his security forces to prepare to take on Iran's most powerful ally in Iraq, Kataib Hezbollah, a group which officials have accused of running a smuggling ring that siphoned off hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of state-owned oil.

articles.title: Iran's proxy in Iraq rakes in hundreds of millions through oil smuggling
articles.description: Kataib Hezbollah, a Shi'ite militia in Iraq, has been accused of stealing state oil for years. Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has launched a crackdown against their smuggling operations, which have robbed the government substantially. Nine officials have been dismissed as a result of a high-level investigation into this smuggling network. The militia denies the allegations and claims the crackdown is politically motivated.

articles.title: Iran’s proxy in Iraq rakes in hundreds of millions through oil smuggling
articles.description: By Ahmed RasheedBAGHDAD, Nov 16 (Reuters) - Iran's most powerful Shi'ite militia ally in Iraq has been raking in hundreds of millions of dollars from oil stolen from the state, Iraqi officials say, prompting the prime minister to ready his security forces to confront the heavily armed group.Prime Minister Alial-Zaidi has launched his toughest challenge yet to the group Kataib Hezbollah by cracking down on an oil smuggling network it has run for years, senior security, army, police and oil officials told Reuters.
